content.text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"application_screening_fees","status":"in_force","title":"California Civil Code Section 1950.6 - Application Screening Fees","requirement":"A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee to cover the costs of obtaining information about the applicant, including personal reference checks and consumer credit reports. The fee shall not exceed $30 per applicant and may be adjusted annually by CPI beginning January 1, 1998. Landlords must not charge when no rental unit is available or will be available within a reasonable period of time. Landlords must provide screening criteria in writing, approve the first applicant meeting criteria, and cannot charge unless the application is actually considered. Landlords must provide a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent. If a screening report is obtained, landlords must provide a copy to the applicant within seven days. Unused portions of fees must be refunded. Landlords must either follow an approved screening process that considers applications in order and approves the first qualified applicant with refunds for concurrent submissions within seven days, or return the entire screening fee within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever is first.","citation":"California Civil Code Section 1950.6(a)-(l), as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67,
